message.content:
**Action taken:** I bought 23 shares of MSFT at a limit of $420.50; the order filled at $420.50 for $9,671.50 total (005:05 UTC quote, last $420.18). This is my only order today, so it uses $9,671.50 of the $20,000 daily cap and stays under the $10,000 per-order cap, within the AAPL/MSFT buy-only mandate, and no cash left the account (remaining cash ≈ $40,328.50 plus the 100 MSFT shares already held).

**Summary:** I read Microsoft's FY2024 Form 10-K (fiscal year ended June 30, 2024, filed July 30, 2024) and concluded a modest, mandate-compliant add was justified: total revenue grew 16% to **$245,122 million** from $211,915 million, with operating income up 24% to $109,433 million, net income up 22% to $88,136 million, diluted EPS of $11.80, and operating cash flow of $118,548 million — a business still compounding at scale, led by Microsoft Cloud revenue of $137.4 billion (+23%) and Azure growth of 30%. Balance-sheet quality supports it too (cash and short-term investments of $75.5 billion, AAA-rated long-term debt), and the main offsets I weighed were heavy AI/datacenter capital spending ($44.5 billion of capex), the $28.9 billion IRS transfer-pricing proposed adjustment, and Activision Blizzard integration losses ($1.36 billion operating loss in the period owned). Because the mandate caps each order at $10,000 and requires a limit near the market, I sized the position at 23 shares at $420.50 against a $420.18 last price rather than taking a larger stake, keeping the order small and the limit tight to the current market.
